text:
- chief complaint: back pain for four days, shifting from the right side to the left.
- history of present illness: the patient reports pain similar to a kidney stone episode two years ago. It was intermittent, became constant and severe over the last 48 hours, and is not relieved by Tylenol. The patient may have blood in the urine. Migraines are well controlled on Imitrex. Reflux is stable with diet changes, though the patient has been ordering more take-out.
- physical examination: elevated blood pressure, right costovertebral angle tenderness, right lower quadrant abdominal tenderness, clear heart and lung sounds. Creatinine is slightly elevated. Abdominal x-ray shows a possible lower kidney stone, pending official read.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: shifting back pain, dizziness and lightheadedness with exertion, abdominal pain, possible hematuria, body aches from favoring the back.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: Ultram 50 mg every six hours as needed for pain (new); Protonix 40 mg daily (refill); Imitrex continued.
- follow-up instructions: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast, to be scheduled by nursing; push fluids and strain urine; doctor will follow up in about a day; call if symptoms worsen.
